input: It is worth considering the performance of the centrifugal pump that moves caustic solution between the two vessels at grade, because the reported figures, taken together, give a fairly complete picture of the intended operating condition. At the duty point, the flow is 86 m3 h-1 against a head of 20 m, with pump efficiency 70%, and the shaft power at the duty point is 6.7 kW. The motor is rated 15% above this value, a margin that is presumably intended to provide a comfortable degree of headroom above the calculated requirement at the selected point. It should also be noted that cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test, which ran for 4 h at the duty point only, and this observation is broadly reassuring as far as it goes. At the same time, the observation is tied to the tested point and to the duration of the test, and it does not in itself say anything about behaviour at other flows or under other suction conditions. The efficiency figure likewise belongs to the duty point, and the wider performance of the pump away from that point is not described by the values given. Overall, the passage presents a single, clearly defined operating point, a motor margin above the shaft power at that point, and an acceptance observation whose reach is limited to the condition actually tested.
target: Caustic solution is moved between two vessels at grade by a centrifugal pump, and the reported duty is a single operating point rather than a curve. At the duty point, flow is 86 m3 h-1 against a head of 20 m, with pump efficiency 70%. Shaft power at the duty point is 6.7 kW. The motor is rated 15% above the shaft power; the margin sets the installed rating, and the margin is not a measured efficiency and does not change the duty-point power. Pump efficiency connects the hydraulic power imparted to the liquid with the shaft power drawn at the same point, and the stated value belongs to that point. The vessels stand at grade, and the stated head is the head the pump works against in the reported arrangement. A selection made from the duty point still depends on the system curve of the connecting line, and no second operating point is reported from which that curve could be drawn. Operation away from the duty point is outside the reported result: a centrifugal pump delivers a different flow and head as system resistance changes, and efficiency moves with them. Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test. The acceptance test ran for 4 h at the duty point only, and the observation is limited to the tested condition. No cavitation statement is made for other flows, other suction conditions, or longer running. The duty figures fix the selection point and the motor margin, and the test result fixes what was seen at that point during acceptance.
